docs.title: Erazure's PD2 Loot Filter
docs.text: A highly stylized loot filter for Project Diablo 2, with multiple filter level tiers for customizable strictness and colorful, intuitive symbols for runes, gems, maps, charms, and more.

docs.title: Get started
docs.text:
1. In the PD2 launcher, open Item Filter Profiles, pick Erazure - Main, and click Save Filter on the right side. Not sure which version? Main is the one to start with; Versions says what the others change.
  2. In game, pick your filter level: Esc > Options > PD2 Options, or the Increase / Decrease Filter Level hotkeys (set them in Configure Controls). Your Horadric Cube's description shows the version and level you're on.
  3. Start on level 1, Lowest Strictness: it's for the ladder start and characters up to level ~80. Move to a stricter level as your character outgrows its drops; Filter Levels shows what each one hides. Not sure which? Which level for me? asks four questions.

The launcher keeps the filter up to date: each update reaches you the next time you press Play. The filter is updated for the Season 14 Alliance ladder; last updated November 27th, 2026 (what's new). Something not working? See Troubleshooting.

How the Erazure loot filter shows non-magical armor and weapons that drop on the ground, read from the filter's own rules. Anything a base's rows don't cover is shown as usual.

Tag a word or mark on the name, and any note it adds to the hover box (shown as the game draws them) Notify minimap icon and chat notification Shows as a display of its own Shown shown as usual: a case a Hidden row lets through Hidden the item is not shown
  • Each row is one case: the filter levels it applies to, what happens, and what the item needs. Every column must hold; any means no condition. Pick your filter level in the bar to see only your rows.
  • ED is enhanced defense on armor and enhanced damage on weapons (superior items). Class items roll +1–3 to skills; a runeword base with several skill combinations opens to list them.
  • Bases of one type and tier with the same socket maximum, size, and rows share a group.
  • Bases for a runeword, under the bar, lists only the bases a runeword fits, under what the finished runeword's label shows.
  • Ethereal weapons with no sockets that a class would corrupt into a rare (bricking) get a red star and a note while you play that class: the Class column names it.
  • Hidden items still show in town. The minimap icon and chat notification come on their own, even for a hidden item. Low quality items (Cracked, Crude, Damaged) have their own rows when they differ.

docs.title: Edit by Hand
docs.text:
The easiest way to change Erazure is the Filter Editor: it builds your own copy in your browser (looks, sounds, items, your own rules) and saves it straight into your game, and your changes carry over to every Erazure update. This page is for editing a copy of the filter file by hand.

A hand-edited copy doesn't update

The launcher's Erazure updates by itself; your own copy stays on the day you downloaded it. After each Erazure update, download the new file and make your edits again. Already have a hand-edited copy and tired of that? Paste the rules you wrote into the Filter Editor's My rules: it adds them to every new Erazure for you.

docs.title: Edit a copy
docs.text:
1. In the launcher, open Item Filter Profiles, pick Erazure and the version you want, and click Copy to Local: it copies that version into Diablo II\ProjectD2\filters\local. (Or download the file from the filter's GitHub page, such as Erazure-Main.filter, and save it in that folder.)
  2. Open the file in your text editor (VS Code or Notepad++), make your edits and save it, as a .filter file.
  3. In the launcher, open Item Filter Profiles, click Local Filter, pick your file and click Save Filter.
  4. In game, press the reload filter key (Numpad 0 unless you changed it in Configure Controls), or start the game.

The file is about 2.4 MB, and some lines are very long: the filter's shorthand (its aliases) is written out in every rule, which makes the game load it faster. The Filter Editor shows Erazure's rules in their short form (Erazure's rules), and its My rules checks each rule you write as the game reads it.

docs.title: Text editors
docs.text:
• VS Code: under File > Preferences > Extensions, search for "TommyC90" and install the Diablo 2 Loot Filter Hints extension. It colors the parts of each rule.
  • Notepad++: open the file with File > Open.

The pictures of items on the ground are Erazure - Main on filter level 1 (potions, scrolls, and tomes for a level 5 character, everything else for level 90); the hover boxes are screenshots from the game. docs.title: Unique and set items
docs.text:
Unidentified on the ground, a unique or set item's look tells its tier; Unique & Set Tiers has every item's.

Left, High value: the bases of Harlequin Crest, Tyrael's Might, Griffon's Eye, and Dracul's Grasp. Middle, Medium value (Lightsabre or Azurewrath, The Grandfather) and Minimal value (Blood Raven's Charge, Lycander's Flank). Right, a Diablo Clone or Rathma unique (Cage of the Unsullied), a unique in no tier, the Grail look of one you haven't discovered yet, and a unique for low level dueling.

Left, High value: Tal Rasha's Guardianship, Natalya's Mark, and Griswold's Honor. Middle, Medium value: M'avina's True Sight, Guillaume's Face, and Aldur's Deception. Right, the standard set look, the dimmer look of a low set item at a high character level, and the Grail look of one you haven't discovered yet.

docs.title: Tags and highlights
docs.text:
Once an item is identified, the line under its name holds the filter's tags: its best stats in short, 30fcr, 45r, and 3mpk (Tags and Symbols explains each). A unique's or set item's tags are its rolls. A line between stars is a highlight (Skill & Shop Highlights lists those on jewelry, armor, weapons, and class items), and notes such as Max Sockets and Upgrade, with its recipe, come under the name too. Screenshots from the game:

A rare ring with the Physical highlight: damage, dexterity, two resistances, and mana after each kill.

Rare boots with the Triple Resist highlight: run speed, life, and three resistances, then their upgrade and the recipe for it.

Rare gloves: cast rate, curse duration, enhanced defense, and maximum mana.

A magic small charm with the Physical highlight: maximum damage, attack rating, and life.

A rare ethereal sword with the Enhanced Damage highlight: its sockets after the name, its runes, and tags for attack speed, enhanced damage, and damage to undead.

A mirrored rare maul: enhanced damage and crushing blow, six sockets of runes, and the Enhanced Damage highlight.

The Stone of Jordan: its rolls (mana, maximum mana) and its corruption's damage reduction, with a highlight.

Death's Web: its poison and bone skills, enemy poison resistance roll, and the corruption's cast rate and fire skill damage.

Guardian Angel: skills and maximum resistances, how many sockets it can still get (L: Larzuk, P: Puzzlebox, C: corruption), and its upgrade with the recipe for it.

Tal Rasha's Guardianship: its magic damage reduction and magic find rolls.

Magic gloves in a shop: their sell value, +3 to Javelin and Spear Skills with 20% attack speed, and the +3/20ias highlight.

docs.title: Maps
docs.text:
An identified map's hover box opens with its tags (experience, monster rarity, monster density, and magic find), then its area level, the highest resistances and the immunities of its monsters, its guest monsters, and its mods to watch out for: gray for a small roll, red for a dangerous one. A high monster rarity or density roll stands between stars, more of them the higher it is. Under them come its experience lines: on an uncorrupted map the tag, 1.80x Experience, is how much more a full clear gives with the map's rolls than without them (is it worth corrupting?), and on every map 2.10x at Level 90 is what it gives you at your level against the average plain T1-T3 map, for the same distance walked. Map Experience explains both. These pictures are from before November 17th, when both numbers had one decimal, corrupted maps showed the tag too, and the lines came in another order.

A rare T1 map: two small rolls in gray, crushing blow in red, +40% Monster Rarity between stars, 1.6x Experience, and 1.8x at level 90.

A rare T2 map with Fetishes as guest monsters, two kinds of extra elemental damage and less chance to block in red, +84% Monster Density between stars, 1.5x Experience, and 1.9x at level 90.

A corrupted rare T3 map: all four tags, +62% Monster Rarity between stars, 1.8x Experience, and 2.1x at level 90. Corrupted, it shows no area level, highest resistances, or small rolls.

docs.title: Filter Levels
docs.text:
Pick your filter level in game: Esc > Options > PD2 Options, or with the Increase / Decrease Filter Level hotkeys (set them in Configure Controls). The Horadric Cube's description says which level you are on.

Super Healing and Super Mana Potions show on every filter level. To hide healing or mana potions on any level, turn on Hide Healing Potions or Hide Mana Potions in the game's Loot Filter options: they hide every healing or mana potion, whatever the filter level.

How to read it

What each filter level of the Erazure loot filter shows, notifies, and hides, for every kind of item that drops, read from the filter's own rules: the table first, then what changes from one level to the next. Pick your level in game (Esc > Options > PD2 Options, or the Increase / Decrease Filter Level hotkeys); the Horadric Cube's description says which level you are on.

  • Shown for Erazure - Main, on the ground outside town in Nightmare and Hell; a cell's details add what Normal difficulty and special areas change.
  • Each column is a group of filter levels that behave the same; levels that differ only in the Rejuvenation Potion (35%) share one (3-4, 5-6).
  • Many items hide only once your character reaches a level: from clvl 80 means from character level 80. The strip under a cell shows character levels 1 to 99, hatched where items hide. Type your character level in the bar to see your own.
  • Click a cell for its details: which items, when, and what changes in Normal difficulty and special areas. The rows link to the pages with every base and item.
  • Hidden items still show in town, and unique and set items still show until you've discovered them (Discovery Progress). Level 0 hides nothing.
  • Unique and set items drop unidentified: one row per value tier. Non-magical items: two rows each, plain (no sockets, not superior, and no skills) and best case (the most a base can show with any sockets, enhanced defense or damage, or skills); the Non-magical Bases page has every base.

docs.text: Type any grail item: its chance per map, the ear that finds it most often, and its best bet, at the bar's settings.

docs.title: Your Grail
docs.text:
Mark the items you've discovered under Every Item, or fill in your grail at the end of this tab: mark everything discovered but what you're missing, or paste a list. From your list and the bar's settings this is your plan: the Corrupted Ear to run, the items one kill finds more often than one whole map and where to farm them, what a unique map's bosses find, and the slowest ones. Every Item shows each missing item's best bet. Your list is kept in this browser only.

Replace my list with it Add its items to my list Leave my list as it is Undo

Clear the dates Share or move your list: Copy a link to your list Copy a picture Save the picture Farm spotsAny farm spotFixed spots only A fixed spot stands in the same place every game (Bone Ash in the Cathedral); a random one anywhere in its area. Every ear for your missing items

The best ear depends on the goal: the most of your missing items in your next 100 maps, 90% of them, or all of them.

Fill in your grail: mark everything discovered, paste a list, or copy your list The names in the box: Mark these discoveredMark these undiscovered Mark all but these discoveredReplace my list Your whole list: Mark all discoveredMark all undiscovered Show my listCopy the names Undo

What the box reads and what each button does
  • Quickest: open the Compendium view and page through it beside the game's own Compendium, clicking the cards you've discovered.
  • Found most of it? Type what you're missing in the box, one name per line, and press "Mark all but these discovered": every other item is marked discovered. In game, the stash's Uniques and Sets tabs list what you're missing when you turn on "Show Undiscovered" (hover an item for its name). Or press "Mark all discovered" and mark the missing ones undiscovered one by one under Every Item: type a name in its search and press Enter.
  • Found a few? Type them in the box and press "Mark these discovered", or click their boxes under Every Item. For a whole set or base at once, search it there and press "Mark listed items discovered".
  • The box's buttons: "Mark these discovered" adds the names to your list, "Mark these undiscovered" takes them off, "Mark all but these discovered" marks every item discovered but the names, and "Replace my list" marks the names discovered and everything else undiscovered.
  • What the box reads: one item per line, from a spreadsheet, another grail tracker, or typed by hand (Harlequin Crest, Arm of King Leoric). Capitals, apostrophes, a leading "The", bullets, numbering, and a checked box such as [x] don't matter, a version in brackets counts as the item (Harlequin Crest (Shako)), and a spreadsheet row counts by the cell with the name. Lines with an empty box ([ ], ✗) and rows marked no, false, 0, or ✗ are skipped, and the lines it doesn't recognize are listed under the buttons (the first 10). Items that don't count for the grail (How It's Worked Out names them) are listed apart.
  • Keep or move your list: "Copy a link to your list", under your plan's cards, copies a link that holds your list: open it in another browser or on another device, and the page there offers to replace its list with yours or add your items to it. To show a friend your grail, send the picture ("Copy a picture" beside it). "Copy the names" copies the names of your discovered items ("Show my list" shows them in the box): paste them into this box in another browser and press "Replace my list".
  • Undo takes back your changes one at a time, latest first, while you stay on the page.

Maps find the most grail items over time. For an item maps rarely drop, killing one boss or superunique again and again can be the better bet. A character that teleports doesn't have to clear its maps: scout a rare map for its map event, do the event, kill the map boss, and open the next map. This planner counts full clears. docs.title: Gambling
docs.text:
Gambling buys an unidentified item of a base you pick, for gold. Each one has a 1 in 2,000 chance to be unique and 1 in 1,000 to be a set item, whatever your magic find, and it counts for your grail like a drop. The table ranks the gamble bases by the gold they take per new grail item: for your missing items once you mark some discovered, else for a fresh grail. docs.title: How It's Worked Out
docs.text:
• The grail: every unique and set item in the game, unique maps, quest items, and nine uniques that don't count for the grail left out (Itherael's Path, Overlord's Helm, Dark Abyss, Aidan's Scar, Hadriel's Hand, Band of Skulls, Cage of the Unsullied, The Third Eye, and Rainbow Facet). An item that comes in several versions (Akarat's Devotion, Cyclopean Roar, and Arm of King Leoric, two versions each) is one grail item: any of its versions finds it, so its chances are those of all its versions together.
  • Drops: each monster's drops and their quality as the game rolls them: each base's chance to be unique or set at the monster's level (class items have their own, better chances), magic find with its diminishing returns, and a unique picked among the base's uniques by their weight. A unique roll on a base with no unique becomes a rare, a set roll with no set item magic.
  • Maps: full clears, averaged over the maps of a tier, from the map model behind the filter's experience tags (monsters per area, elite packs, and monster levels; the website's Map Experience page explains it). "Rare" is the average rare map with a corruption: its density, monster rarity, and magic find. Solo; one map boss per map, each map's own: its own loot at its own level (80 to 91; map bosses keep their level as other bosses do).
  • The Bitter Depths: the map event in about 1 rare T1-T3 map in 26 and 1 non-magical map in 82 (its portal always opens, late in the clear). Its 20 Lucion's chests drop as a tier-0 vault's do, 5 items each; its monsters (5 elite packs) and Zoltun Kulle drop as map monsters do, and your ear works on them, not on the chests. The map's magic find carries into it, for the chests too. Zoltun's death also sets off a treasure explosion: his loot again and again until 60 items lie on the ground, at his level, with no magic find (your ear doesn't touch it either). Its 7 sparkly chests are left out (about 3% of its chests' grail drops). Every map's numbers include it at that chance.
  • Cow King's Leathers: only a Hell Bovine's drop can be one of its pieces: the cows of the Secret Cow Level and the Cow King. Blood Moon's cows are other monsters and never drop it. Maps have Hell Bovines two ways, and the page counts both for these three items: the Bovine guest ("Map contains Hell Bovines"), a prefix on about 1 rare T1 map in 18 and 1 rare T2 or T3 map in 28, which adds the cows to every area's monsters (in groups and elite packs, beside the map's own) with +25-30% density and +15-20% magic find; and the Dark Wanderer map event, whose three wanderers each turn into a random act boss or superunique: the Cow King, with his 8 Hell Bovines, in about 1 rare map in 260 and 1 non-magical map in 800 (an event always brings all three).
  • Grail progress: each item drops at random at its own rate, so the items found after n maps add up item by item. "Switching" works from the expected progress; with your real list the planner does better.
  • Farm spots: one kill of each act boss and superunique in each difficulty, solo: the monster's own drop at its own level. The drops of the minions around a superunique are counted apart, as "with its minions". In Normal difficulty a monster has a fixed level of its own; in Nightmare and Hell it takes the area's level, but bosses keep theirs; superuniques and their minions are 3 levels higher. A kill makes at most six items, gold and potions included, so Duriel's many drop rolls always end at six. A boss drops its quest loot only while the quest is open; farming kills drop the usual loot.
  • Spots: "fixed" means the monster stands in the same place every game: its area is one of the game's preset maps (the Cathedral, Tower Cellar Level 5, Nihlathak's Temple...), or laid out the same way every game (Travincal, the Chaos Sanctuary, the Bloody Foothills), or it waits in a piece the game always puts at the same edge of its area (Eldritch by the Bloody Foothills, Stormtree in the Flayer Jungle at its border with Lower Kurast). The others stand in a piece of the area the game places anywhere in it. "Areas from a waypoint" counts the areas to walk through from the nearest waypoint (towns have one; portals count as one step).
  • Corrupted Zones: in Hell games made with Baal's quest done, one group of areas at a time has area level 85, so its superuniques are level 88 (bosses keep their own level).
  • Ubers and events:
    • Lilith, Uber Duriel, and Uber Izual drop their own loot at level 110.
    • Diablo Clone drops Annihilus every kill; Uber Tristram drops the Hellfire Torch once a run, when its last boss dies (the three bosses drop nothing else).
    • The Uber Ancients: before touching the altar you switch on the ancients you want to fight at their statues, one, two, or all three; the altar then drops 20 to 29 items for one ancient, 32 to 47 for two, and 44 to 65 for three, at item level 90.
    • Lucion's vault has 10 chests at every tier (0, 1, and 2, easiest first); each drops 3 items, then 2, 3, or 4 more from better loot on tier 0, 1, or 2, so a harder tier gives more items, not better ones. The items have the vault's level (89); the level of the character who opens the chest (95 here) goes into their quality. The numbers are for the whole vault; Lucion himself drops no grail items.
    • The vault's key is cubed from three parts, each a chance per kill in Hell (Lucion's Chests names them; solo, as every number here).
  • Unique map bosses: the bosses of four unique maps drop extra loot when they die, on top of their own. Unique maps open only in Hell, one a game; one run a map, and the rest of the map isn't counted.
    • Three drop random uniques: Gregus Mazi in City of Ureh 3 (socketed), Warlord of Blood 2 or 3 (corrupted), and Na-Krul in Na-Krul's Abyss 3 (ethereal, but for the indestructible ones).
    • Each starts as a unique picked at random, every unique alike but the few with no rarity (Embersworn among them; Rainbow Facets are in; Gregus Mazi passes over bases that take no sockets). Na-Krul drops the unique he picked.
    • Warlord of Blood and Gregus Mazi keep only its base and make a unique of it at item level 99, picked as any dropped unique is, by how common each unique of that base is (one already dropped in the game comes out rare).
    • Their own loot drops as a map boss's does, at their level (91), with the map's own magic find.
    • Djinn's Domain's two Djinns, Siren of the Forgotten Vault and Djinn of a Thousand Blades, each set off a treasure explosion when they die: their own loot again and again until 60 items lie on the ground, at their level (90), with no magic find. Their own loot drops too, twice (Djinn's Domain repeats every monster's drop) and a third time half the time (the map's extra drop).
    • The minibosses (Zayl the Merciful in City of Ureh; Cory the Imp and Onion the Accused in Warlord of Blood) drop only their own loot, as their map's boss does (level 91). A run counts it: players kill them too.
  • T4 dungeons: one run a dungeon, a whole clear of its two floors, the average of the three dungeons. The cube makes them rare: an average rare dungeon with a corruption (+148% density, +27% monster rarity, and +161% magic find on top of yours).
    • Every monster killed in a T4 dungeon drops its own loot twice, the bosses too; a unique monster's minions drop theirs once.
    • Its two bosses, one on its first floor and one on its last, each set off a treasure explosion when they die: the first floor's boss until 30 items lie on the ground, the last floor's until 60, at the boss's level (92; Skullsplitter Cyrus 90), with no magic find. Their loot, explosions and own alike, is the Uber Ancients' altar's. The three dungeons' bosses drop alike.
    • Dungeons are deadly: every monster has several immunities, so few builds can clear one, and a dungeon can take upwards of 45 minutes to an hour or longer. The page weighs a dungeon against the full map clears 45 minutes to an hour holds (15 minutes each, the estimated time of Map Event and Boss Rushing).
  • Best bet: an item's best bet compares one kill with one map: target farming its best boss or superunique (any difficulty; Corrupted Zones, ubers, events, unique map bosses, and T4 dungeon bosses left out) when one kill there finds it at least as often as a whole map with the item's best ear, maps otherwise. That's as if a kill took as long as a map; a quicker kill makes farming better still. Your Grail's plan sorts your missing items by it, and splits the maps' ones by their chance in your next 100 maps with the ear it names: an even chance or better, or the slowest.
  • Gheed's map event (its tab): each of his 5 offers is a random unique: any unique but jewels and the few with no rarity (Embersworn among them). One that needs character level 60 or more is turned down (level − 49)% of the time and another picked; in one shop in 200, one offer is a special ring instead.
  • Gambling: each gambled item's item level is your character level −5 to +4. The base becomes exceptional with a chance that grows 0.9% per item level above the exceptional version's level, else elite with 0.33% per level above the elite version's (only once the exceptional chance is above zero). Then it is unique 1 time in 2,000 and a set item 1 time in 1,000, picked among the uniques or sets of that base whose level is at most the item level, like a drop; with none, the roll is lost. Magic find plays no part. The gold: rings 50,000, amulets 63,000; any other base costs more the higher your character level, and the more so the higher its exceptional and elite versions' prices (no reduced vendor prices here). Cow King's Leathers never comes from gambling. Gambling ranks the bases.
  • Magic find: the bar is your character's magic find. Unique, set, and rare chances grow with it, ever slower (the game's diminishing returns). A map's own magic find adds to yours before them, as the game does: ; the unique maps add their own.
  • Left out:
    • The rest of a unique map (only its bosses count).
    • The map events but the Bitter Depths (Treasure Fallen, Corrupted Heroes, Horazon, the Dark Wanderer, and the rest; Gheed's shop has its own tab), and map guests. Cow King's Leathers alone counts the Bovine guest and the Dark Wanderer's Cow King. The website's Map Event and Boss Rushing page counts every event.
    • A rare map's extra weapon, armor, and crafting drops (some of its suffixes).
    • Magic maps, Fortified maps, and parties (the notes on the Corrupted Ears tab say what the last two change).
    • Whole area clears: a full Cow Level, Chaos Sanctuary, or Baal run also drops from every monster on the way, so those runs find more than the boss alone shows here.
    • PD2's special drops (sigils, Corrupted Zone shards) aren't grail items.
Words on this page 1 in 1,200 mapsA chance, not a promise: on average one drop every 1,200 full map clears. A 90% chance to see the item takes about 2.3 times that many; luck runs ahead or behind. Kills, runs, maps, dungeons, vaults, shops, gamblesFarm spots count per kill; per run for Uber Tristram and the Uber Ancients (one, two, or three ancients, your choice at their statues); per map for the unique map bosses (one run of the map); per dungeon for a T4 dungeon (a whole one, or its two bosses); per vault (its 10 chests) for Lucion's vault; per shop for Gheed's map event; per gamble (with its gold) for gambling; per run for the Bitter Depths (its chests, monsters, and Zoltun Kulle), which every map's numbers count at the event's chance. A kill and a map clear take very different times, so compare spots with spots and maps with maps. No ear, Any ear, Best earAn item's chance per map without a Corrupted Ear, with an ear whose pool doesn't have the item's base (what every ear gives), and with the ear whose pool has it. Best ear ×How many times more often the best ear finds an item than no ear. Maps for 90%The maps for a 90% chance to see an item. Best betWhere an item comes from best: target farming its best boss or superunique when one kill there finds it at least as often as a whole map (on rare maps, with its best ear: non-magical maps take none; "beats maps"), maps otherwise. A kill = 3 mapsOne kill finds the item as often as 3 maps with its best ear: farming wins as long as a kill takes you less time than 3 maps. Drop levelThe lowest monster level that can drop an item: not the level you need to wear it. The farm spots reach level 68 in Normal and 75 in Nightmare, so the highest-level items only come from Hell. Normal, Nightmare, HellThe difficulties. A "normal base" (beside exceptional and elite) is an item's base tier. Fixed spot, random spotA fixed spot is the same every game (the Cathedral, Travincal, Nihlathak's Temple); a random one is anywhere in its area. Areas from a waypointThe areas to walk through from the nearest waypoint (towns have one; a portal counts as one step). With its minionsA superunique's own drop is the main number; "with its minions" adds the monsters around it. Corrupted ZoneIn Hell games made with Baal's quest done, one group of areas at a time has area level 85, so its superuniques drop at level 88 while the zone lasts. Ubers and eventsLilith, Uber Duriel, Uber Izual, Diablo Clone, Uber Tristram, the Uber Ancients, and Lucion's vault. A modelThe numbers follow how the game rolls drops (what each monster can drop, its quality, and magic find) and the map model behind the filter's experience tags, solo: estimates, not a drop log.

All tiersNormalExceptionalElite How to read this page: the rows, the columns, and the filter levels How to read it

How the Erazure loot filter shows magic items that drop on the ground, unidentified, read from the filter's own rules. At the filter levels a base's rows don't cover, it shows with its plain name in blue, with Eth before it when it is ethereal.

Notify minimap icon and chat notification, and a drop sound where one is shown Shows as a look of its own (shown as the game draws it) Hidden the item is not shown
  • Each row is one case: the filter levels it applies to, what happens, and what the item needs. Every column must hold; any means no condition. Pick your filter level in the bar to see only your rows.
  • Crafted affix level is the affix level the filter works out for a craft made from the item: from half your character level plus half its item level.
  • Bases of one type and tier with the same socket maximum and rows share a group. A look shows the group's first base; each base shows its own name.
  • Hidden items still show in town. The minimap icon and chat notification come on their own, even for a hidden item.
  • Charms drop only as magic items (the game has no rare charms). The number after the dot in a charm's look is its item level; a row shows its lowest.

docs.title: Minimal Version
docs.text:
Pick Minimal in the launcher (or one of its Revealed, BIG GG, and PoE versions), then click Save Filter on the right side.

Minimal is Erazure - Main with a minimal style: fewer, simpler symbols around the names of items. Everything else is the same as Main: the filter levels, which items show or hide, the notifications, the minimap icons, and the drop sounds.

These are the labels that look different, drawn as the game draws them. The Horadric Cube shows as the version's name.

docs.title: Skill & Shop Highlights
docs.text:
A highlight is a line of stars the filter adds to an item's hover box (+3/20ias, +7 Chain Lightning); in a shop some items also get a green or teal Cost line. Pick your class in the bar.

Physical rings

either Minimum and Maximum Damage together 20+ and one of: Attack Rating 80+, any Life Stolen per Hit, any Mana Stolen per Hit, All Resistances 8%+, Strength 10+, Dexterity 10+, Life 20+, Vitality 8+, any Faster Run/Walk, all Attributes 4+, Half Freeze Duration, Magic Find 15%+, Faster Cast Rate 10%+, Mana after each Kill 3+, Life after each Kill 3+, Telekinesis charges, or any Physical Damage Reduction; or Attack Rating 101+, Life Stolen per Hit 5%+, All Resistances 8%+, and Maximum Damage 11+ or Minimum Damage 6+

Caster rings

Faster Cast Rate 20%+

Worth selling, less: 10,000 to 19,999 gold below character level 60

$12k

Its sell price in thousands of gold (12k = 12,000), in Normal below character level 30

LLD

Good for Low Level Dueling (PvP at character level 30 and below)

How to read a tag
  • The number is the item's own roll (or its total, a roll plus its runes): 20fcr on a ring is 20% faster cast rate.
  • The letters say which stat it is; the card's title writes the number as #. Some letters mean more than one stat and the color tells them apart: #r is fire resistance in red, cold in blue, lightning in yellow, and poison in green.
  • The color: where a tag comes in more than one color for a kind of item, the color says how good the roll is. Each card draws the tag in each of its looks at the lowest value that look takes, with the values beside it (30+: from 30; 10–29; any: at any value).
  • The kinds of item above a tag all show it that way; where the color or the values differ, a kind has a line of its own.
  • Tags show once an item is identified.

Version Uniques & setsUniquesSets Sets by item typeSets by set More filters How to read this page: the tiers, the filter levels, and the items in no tier How to read it

How the Erazure loot filter shows unique and set items that drop unidentified: the tier each one is in, and when the others are shown quietly or hidden. Everything here is read from the filter's own rules. Once identified, an item shows its own name and the tags of its rolls: open Once identified under an item to see them.

  • Each line is one case: when it applies, the tier, the label as the game draws it, the minimap icon, and the drop sound. A tier named alone notifies as usual (see Tiers); otherwise the difference follows in brackets.
  • Press ▶ beside a sound to hear it. Point at the sound for its number: type .playsound and that number in game to hear it there.
  • Items on the same base share a tier. Unidentified, the filter cannot tell them apart: Lightsabre and Azurewrath are both a Phase Blade.
  • Hidden items still show their name in town. Until you've discovered an item (the Holy Grail Discovery Progress) it is never hidden and always gets a minimap icon and a chat notification when it drops, on every filter level, and a drop sound (its own, or the Grail sound where it has none), and wherever it isn't High or Medium value (set rings and amulets too) it shows the Grail look: an orange star on each side (a Minimal value unique and a Medium value set item have a Grail look of their own). An item on a base with several uniques, like Thunder Maul, counts as discovered once you've found all of them.
  • The game's Force Show Unowned option (in its Loot Filter options, off by default) also shows the ones you have discovered but don't own yet where the filter would hide them, with the game's plain name instead of these looks.
Filter levels Tiers

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Something not working as you expected? Most questions players ask come down to one of these. Still stuck after them? Send a report about the item, or message erazure on Discord.

docs.title: Which version and filter level am I on?
docs.text: Hover over your Horadric Cube: its description shows the filter's version, the date of its last update (for example Season 14 - November 21st - v2), and the filter level you're on. Compare the date with What's New to see whether you have the newest update.

docs.title: The filter didn't update
docs.text:
• The launcher downloads the filter each time you press Play. Right after an update it can still hand out the old file for up to about 5 minutes: close the game, wait a few minutes, and press Play again.
  • The first time you pick Erazure, click Save Filter after picking the version in Item Filter Profiles.
  • If the launcher's Item Filter Profiles shows Local Filter, you're playing your own copy, and it doesn't update by itself. A copy made in the Filter Editor updates when you open the editor and save again; a hand-edited copy needs the new file and your edits again (Edit by Hand).

docs.title: Where do I change the filter level?
docs.text: In game: Esc > Options > PD2 Options, or the Increase / Decrease Filter Level hotkeys (set them in Configure Controls). Level 0 shows every item; levels 1 to 12 go from the least strict to the most. Filter Levels shows what each one hides, and Home says where to start. Not sure which level? Which level for me? asks four questions.

docs.title: My healing or mana potions are gone
docs.text: The game's own Loot Filter options Hide Healing Potions and Hide Mana Potions hide every healing or mana potion, on every filter level, level 0 too, and in your belt, inventory, and shops as well. Turn them off in the game's options. Super Healing and Super Mana Potions show on every Erazure filter level.

docs.title: An item shows that should be hidden
docs.text:
Look it up in the Item Lookup: pick your version, filter level, and character, and it shows the item's label, minimap icon, drop sound, and the rule that decides.

  • Erazure hides items only on the ground outside town. In town, in your inventory, in your stash, and in shops every item shows its name.
  • A unique or set item you haven't discovered yet always shows: Erazure never hides one, and the game's Force Show Undiscovered option (on by default) shows it too.
  • Level 0 hides nothing.

docs.title: An item is hidden that I wanted to see
docs.text: Look it up in the Item Lookup: pick your version, filter level, and character, and it shows the item's label, minimap icon, drop sound, and the rule that decides. Unique & Set Tiers, Non-magical Bases, Magic Items, and Rare Items show on which filter levels and at which character levels each one hides. A less strict filter level shows it, or the Filter Editor can show that one item on the level you play.

docs.title: No drop sound or chat notification
docs.text:
First check the game's own settings: Esc > Options > PD2 Options > Loot Filter. Chat Notifications and Drop Sounds both have to be On for the filter's drop sounds to play, and Chat Notifications for its chat notifications.

On stricter filter levels some items keep their minimap icon but lose their drop sound and chat notification, so fewer alerts come up. The item pages say which items sound on which levels. The Corrlorized versions leave out the minimap icons and drop sounds of some items, among them magic jewels, Large Charms, and rare rings, belts, and boots; Icons and Sounds lists every sound and its items. If an item makes no sound on any level, check the game's sound volume.

docs.title: A label is cut off
docs.text: The game shows at most 56 characters of an item's name on the ground. Erazure keeps its labels within that; if you see one cut off, report it with the item.

docs.title: I changed my own filter, but nothing changed in game
docs.text: The game reads the file only after you save it and press the reload filter key (Numpad 0 unless you changed it in Configure Controls), or start a new game. A Filter Editor change reaches the game only when you save it to the game again.

docs.title: The website shows a different look than my version
docs.text: Most item pages show Erazure - Main; the Item Lookup can show any version, and Unique & Set Tiers any Erazure or Minimal one. The Minimal and Corrlorized versions draw some items with other symbols or colors (Minimal Version shows its differences). Which items show and hide is the same in every version, except that the Corrlorized versions hide small gold piles from lower character levels.

docs.title: Versions of the Filter
docs.text: Not sure? Pick Erazure - Main. Every other version is Main with a different look, or with one or more of three changes added.

docs.title: Pick one in the launcher
docs.text:
1. In the PD2 launcher, open Item Filter Profiles and pick Erazure in the list of authors.
  2. Click a version, then Save Filter on the right side.
  3. In game, hover your Horadric Cube: its description names the version, your filter level, and the date of the update you have. Pick your filter level in game too (Filter Levels says how).

The launcher keeps the filter up to date: each update reaches you the next time you press Play, with no need to save again.

docs.title: What the versions change
docs.text:
A version is a look plus any of three changes; every combination is in the launcher.

Look Erazure The colorful symbols around item names (see them in game). Minimal The same filter with fewer, simpler symbols (every label that differs). Corrlorized Corr's restyle: his own colors, symbols, and Path of Exile sound picks, with the same filter levels. Only with PoE. Add What it changes Revealed Unidentified unique and set items show their identified names when they drop. BIG GG - Mystery The best drops hide what they are on the ground, outside town: BIG GG for Sur, Ber, Jah, Cham, Zod, Vial of Lightsong, Lilith's Mirror, Horadric Almanac, and the Diablo Clone and Rathma uniques; LIL GG for Vex, Ohm, Lo, Larzuk's Puzzlebox, Horadric Navigator, Demonic Cube, and Skeleton Key. You find out when you pick it up. PoE Path of Exile sound effects on valuable drops.

docs.title: See them side by side
docs.text:
The same drops in each look, plain, with Revealed, or with BIG GG, drawn as the game draws them. Click a label to hear its drop sound, in that version and in its PoE one.

Every version as the launcher describes it Version Description Erazure - Main Highly stylized loot filter with multiple filter level tiers for customizable strictness, colorful and intuitive symbols for runes, gems, maps, charms, etc. Erazure - Revealed Same as Erazure - Main but unidentified unique and set items show as their identified names when dropped. Erazure - BIG GG - Mystery Same as Erazure - Main but with a twist: high runes and super rare drops hide their identity on the ground when dropped, showing as BIG GG until you pick them up. Erazure - Revealed - BIG GG Same as Erazure - BIG GG but unidentified unique and set items show as their identified names when dropped. Erazure - Main - PoE Same as Erazure - Main but with Path of Exile sound effects on valuable drops. Polished visuals and tiered, customizable filter levels enhanced with PoE-style sound notifications. Erazure - BIG GG - PoE The mystery of BIG GG drops combined with Path of Exile sound notifications. Minimal - BIG GG - Mystery Same as Minimal but with a twist: high runes and super rare drops hide their identity on the ground when dropped, showing as BIG GG until you pick them up. Minimal - Revealed - BIG GG Same as Minimal - BIG GG but unidentified unique and set items show as their identified names when dropped. Damage Calculator¶

Is that new weapon really an upgrade?

Enter your build, copy it, change one thing, and see what it's worth:

  • Fire, lightning, cold, magic, and poison damage on your attacks, against the monster's resistances and immunities

  • How long a monster or boss takes to die, from a normal map monster to Diablo Clone and Lucion
  • Your builds fighting it to the kill, side by side, drawn as the game draws them: The Fight

  • Boots, belts, amulets, or any other slot, with the rest of your build the same: Compare gear

Season 14 · Cast rate · Hit recovery · Block

How many frames your character takes to cast, to recover from a hit, and to block, at your faster cast rate, faster hit recovery, and faster block rate, and how much more each next frame needs. Attack speed has its own page: the IAS Calculator.

Reset to the defaultsCopy a link to this setup

Character Weapon Holy Shield OffOn Chilled NoYes

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• Frames are the game's, 25 a second: 9 frames is 0.36 seconds.
  • Each stat is diminished: what counts is 120 × your % ÷ (120 + your %), so every breakpoint needs more than the one before.
  • Cast rate stops at 75 of that (about 200% faster cast rate): past the last row, more does nothing.
  • Chilled (by cold damage), you lose up to 50% faster cast rate while it lasts.
  • Holy Shield doubles a Paladin's block speed: 86% faster block rate is then 1 frame.
  • A map's −% hit recovery comes off your faster hit recovery: Map Lines says when its line shows for you.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• One try. A corrupted item can't be corrupted again, and nothing takes a corruption off.
  • Sockets. An item that gets sockets gets as many as the outcome says, at most what its base can hold at its item level.
  • Turns into a rare. The item is gone: a new rare item of the same base takes its place, with new random affixes. On a non-magical item that is often the point of corrupting it (bricking).
  • Desecrated amulets (from Lucion) can turn rare; how likely depends on Lucion's tier. Otherwise they get one of the amulets' rarest outcomes: +1 to All Skills, +10% Faster Cast Rate, +10% Faster Run/Walk, Curse Resistance +10%, +30-40% Enhanced Damage, Cannot Be Frozen, +2% to all Maximum Resistances, or All Resistances +7-10.
  • Maps corrupt with their own odds: each outcome adds its map stats, and the rest of the roll turns the map into a unique map. The lines the filter writes under a map's name for those stats, and when each shows: Map Lines.

docs.title: Damage Calculator
docs.text:
Season 14 · Physical and elemental damage · Attack speed

Compare up to four attack builds against any boss or map monster: damage per second, kill time, attack speed breakpoints, and what each stat is worth.

Pick an example in Start from… on a card, then put in your own numbers. Under each part of a build, what it makes; at the bottom of the screen, every build’s damage per second. Build A, the first card, is the one the others are compared with. To weigh weapons for one character, switch to Compare weapons; boots, belts, amulets, and the rest of your gear, to Compare gear. To fill in a weapon you have, hover over it in game, press Ctrl+C, and paste it into Paste a weapon from the game at the top of its Weapon section.

Your character, skill, gear, and buffs go in the first card; every weapon card uses them and has only the weapon’s own fields, with what it does under them. Weapon A is the one the others are compared with. To fill in a weapon you have, hover over it in game, press Ctrl+C, and paste it into Paste a weapon from the game at the top of its card.

Your build goes in the card, wearing what you wear now. Pick a slot, then in Now the item you wear there (it comes off for the other columns), and up to three items to try instead: each column is your build wearing that item, with the rest the same. Pick an item from the list (its best rolls to start, each roll a box), paste one copied in game (hover over it and press Ctrl+C), or type the stats of a rare. A character loaded from the PD2 armory fills in Now.

Undo

Fields marked ● gold differ from build A (on builds of A’s class).

Every number behind each build’s damage per second. The best of a row is marked.

Average hit: the damage a hit does on average, with critical and deadly strikes counted at their chance. Damage per second counts every hit an attack makes; crushing blow is in the kill time only, since it takes a share of the monster’s life left.

docs.title: Attack speed breakpoints
docs.text: The increased attack speed each build needs on its other gear for each frame count of its attack (its weapon’s IAS as set; its skills’ attack speed and its weapon’s speed counted), and its damage per second there.
